subject: European data transfer: TIA/UK-IDTA clarifications and subprocessor evidence
messages:
From: Sophie Laurent <sophie.laurent@globex.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Globex DPA <dpa@globex.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: European data transfer: TIA/UK-IDTA clarifications and subprocessor evidence

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our procurement review for the upcoming contract we need to confirm a few items related to cross-border transfers and subprocessors before legal can clear the DPA:

- Can Redwood execute EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) + the UK IDTA/UK Addendum? If you have a canonical set, please send.
- We need a TIA/DTIA template or confirmation you will accept a TIA referencing the SCCs.
- Please provide the current subprocessor inventory (including region/data center locations) and whether those subprocessors have been assessed for SCC compliance.
- Do you offer contractual data localization or region-only hosting (we may require EU-only routing for certain data sets)?
- Please attach SOC 2 / relevant security artifacts and a timeline to return our redlines.

We are hoping to close contract review by the end of next week; a 2–3 business day turnaround for requested materials would be ideal. Can we schedule a quick 30-minute call to walk through any gaps?

Best,
Sophie Laurent
Head of Privacy, Globex Corporation
Sophie.Laurent@globex.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Laurent <sophie.laurent@globex.com>
Cc: Globex DPA <dpa@globex.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 12:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: European data transfer: TIA/UK-IDTA clarifications and subprocessor evidence

Hi Sophie —

Thanks, and great to meet you (virtually). High level answers and materials below; attaching the canonical docs as requested.

Attachments (sent):
- Redwood_SCCs_v1.2.pdf (SCCs + controller/processor notes)
- UK-IDTA-Addendum-draft.docx (draft addendum for UK transfers)
- Subprocessors_inventory_2026-08-17.csv (current list, region column included)

Quick answers:
- Execution: We can sign SCCs for EU transfers and the UK IDTA addendum for UK transfers. We typically execute the customer-facing DPA + SCCs and provide the UK addendum as a mutually executed attachment.
- TIA/DTIA: We can provide a TIA template; in many cases a short DTIA that references the SCCs is sufficient. I attached the template as part of the SCCs PDF.
- Subprocessors: The inventory lists all subprocessors and region of operations (AWS eu-west-1, GCP europe-west, content-delivery vendors, analytics vendors). For infrastructure providers, we rely on their contractual and SOC evidence; for software vendors we include attestations where available.
- Data localization: We offer a Dedicated EU deployment option (reserved capacity in EU regions) for customers who require it; otherwise hosted API traffic may route through multi-region endpoints with routing controls.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report is available to customers under NDA — we can share a read-only report link or execute an NDA if needed.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review our draft UK IDTA and flag any redlines; Sohjin/Privacy team is looped below for detailed comments.
2) If you need DocuSign for the addendum, we can prepare it once redlines are agreed.
3) If you require upfront proof of subprocessors' SCC adherence, tell us which vendors you want evidence for and we'll collect the relevant artifacts (3–5 business days typical).

Looping in Soojin Lee (Privacy) and Karthik Iyer (Sales) so they are aware and can help with any commercial/technical constraints.

Best regards,

Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0148

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0400
Subject: Internal: Globex — quick redline priorities for UK-IDTA and subprocessors

Mina / Karthik —

Thanks for the heads-up, Mina. A few internal notes I recommend we raise in the initial round with Globex: 

1) UK-IDTA redlines (priority):
   - Clarify that Redwood will adopt the UK Addendum as provided, but limit indemnity/liability related to international transfers to the cap stated in the main DPA (do not accept open-ended additional caps).
   - Add explicit language that Redwood may rely on subprocessors but will remain contractually responsible for their acts (standard subprocessor liability clause).

2) Subprocessor evidence approach:
   - For cloud infra (AWS, GCP), provide SOC 2 + official compliance pages instead of vendor SCC copies (vendor SCCs are not always provided to customers).
   - For second/third-tier SaaS vendors (analytics, monitoring), provide attestations or a summary of controls. If Globex requests signed SCCs from those vendors specifically, escalate — typical turnaround is 7–10 business days.

3) Commercial fallback: If Globex insists on EU-only processing for the entire account, we should offer Dedicated EU deployment with a 6–8 week lead to provision and a small migration services fee. Karthik, can you confirm if this is acceptable pricing-wise and timeline-wise?

I suggest we return the draft addendum with tracked comments and propose a short call with their privacy/legal team tomorrow or Wednesday.

Sooj

Soojin Lee
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

From: Sophie Laurent <sophie.laurent@globex.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Globex DPA <dpa@globex.com>, Arthur Mendes <arthur.mendes@globex.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: European data transfer: TIA/UK-IDTA clarifications and subprocessor evidence

Thanks, Mina — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few follow-ups from our side (listing our legal team's asks):

- We reviewed the draft UK addendum and will return redlines inline — our outside counsel flagged a couple of liability and breach-notice timing items. Can you accept a limited modification to the liability cap specific to transfer violations?
- For subprocessors: please provide SCC-equivalent language or evidence for the monitoring/analytics vendors (we require vendor-level transfer assurances for any processor that persists or analyzes personal data).
- SOC 2: we'd prefer a direct read-only link rather than an NDA process if possible; can Redwood provide a hosted SOC summary page?
- DocuSign: please prepare the UK addendum for signature; we will route internally once we get your finalized language.

Also, please confirm availability for a 30-minute call tomorrow (Aug 19) at 10:00 AM BST / 05:00 AM EDT to go through the redlines and timeline.

Thanks — attaching our internal DPA redlines for reference.

Best,
Sophie

Subject: Re: European data transfer: TIA/UK-IDTA clarifications and subprocessor evidence

Sophie —

Thanks for the quick review and for sending your redlines. Summary and proposed next steps below so we have a single source of truth:

What Redwood provided (links/attachments):
- Redwood_SCCs_v1.2.pdf (includes our TIA template) — attachment above and hosted copy: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-redwood-sccs
- UK-IDTA-Addendum-draft.docx (tracked comments OK; we expect to negotiate a handful of items)
- Subprocessors_inventory_2026-08-17.csv (CSV lists vendor, role, region, controls link)
- SOC 2: we can provide a hosted SOC summary page to shorten timelines — see internal link. Full report available under NDA.

Globex asks we will address in round 1:
- Liability cap for transfer violations: Redwood can accept a narrowly tailored modification tied to transfer-specific damages, but we need to keep the aggregate DPA cap intact. We will propose language to that effect in tracked changes.
- Subprocessor evidence: We'll prioritize collecting vendor-level attestations for monitoring/analytics vendors. If specific vendors are required for signed SCCs, we will escalate to vendor teams (3–10 business days).
- DocuSign: I will prepare a DocuSign envelope for the UK addendum once we finalize language (target: draft in 48 hours).

Commercial/ops note: looping in Karthik — if Globex requires Dedicated EU deployment, please confirm commercial terms and provisioning ETA so we can include that option in our reply.

Next steps / timeline:
1) Redwood to return tracked UK-IDTA redlines and proposed language on liability (48 hours).
2) Redwood privacy to collect vendor attestations for the five named analytics/monitoring vendors (3–7 business days).
3) DocuSign envelope prepared after redlines agreed (target within 48–72 hours after agreement).

If that timeline works for you, I will prepare the tracked changes and the DocuSign envelope and propose slots for the 30-minute call tomorrow at 10:00 AM BST / 05:00 AM EDT.

Best,

Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
